title: On-demand trace tail retrieval API for cross-storage backfills (Tempo + coldstore)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When traces age out of our hot Tempo store and are archived to S3 coldstore, developers and SREs lose the ability to quickly retrieve the most-recent tail of a trace for post-mortem and latency debugging. Current backfill jobs restore large ranges but are slow and resource intensive.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, on-demand 'trace tail retrieval' API that can fetch the last N spans or last T minutes of a given trace across both Tempo (hot) and S3 coldstore (archived) with schema-aware merging, minimal cost, and auth controls. The API will be used by Console trace viewer, incident runbooks, and debug tooling.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement bulk historical rehydration workflows or change retention policies. It also does not replace full forensic backfills which remain offline jobs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New endpoint GET /v1/traces/{trace_id}/tail?samples=50 or ?minutes=15 returns merged ordered spans from hot and cold storage within 300ms (hot-only) and <5s for mixed fetches.
2) Response includes origin metadata (tempo|coldstore) per span and a canonical timeline.
3) Endpoint enforces RBAC via existing tenant tokens and logs usage for billing.
4) Unit and integration tests cover: tempo-only, coldstore-only, and hybrid paths; schema mismatches; missing trace id; 404 semantics.
5) Console dev flow surfaces tail view and links to full backfill job when available.
technical_notes:
Architecture: introduce a lightweight TailFetcher service that queries Tempo (OTLP/HTTP) for the hot window and queries S3 coldstore via index+range scan using the existing cold index format. The fetcher will: 1) attempt tempo lookup first (fast path), 2) consult cold index for missing time ranges, 3) stream merge by span.timestamp, and 4) attach metadata tags for 'origin' and 'fetch_latency_ms'.

Optimizations: use prefix index on coldstore keys (tenant/traceid/day) to avoid full scans; limit cold reads to at most X MB or Y spans and return a partial flag. Implement a small in-memory LRU cache for recent tail lookups to reduce S3 requests for hot rehydration storms.

Schema handling: implement a tolerant span normalizer that maps legacy Jaeger fields to our canonical OTLP-like JSON shape. Add warnings array in response if fields were migrated or omitted.

Security: endpoint must validate tenant token and honor per-tenant coldstore access policy. Coldstore reads must use rotated read-only credentials via the credential manager (ENG-152601).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature flag behind 'trace_tail_api' gate. 2) Deploy TailFetcher to observability-prod cluster in canary (5% of traffic) and monitor error rates/latency. 3) Enable Console integration for internal users only. 4) Gradually ramp to 100% after 72h with SLOs met. 5) Post-rollout: schedule a review to consider exposing to customers and adding billing metrics.

Monitoring/alerts: error rate > 1% or median latency increase > 25% for tail requests triggers pager to oncall-observability.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for tempo + cold index lookup logic.
- Integration test harness using minio-backed coldstore fixture and local tempo instance with synthetic traces.
- Load test simulating tail fetch storm (1k requests/min) to measure S3 read amplification and cold index latency.
- Security pen-test for tenant isolation and coldstore credential usage.
- Add a test to ensure 'partial' flag when cold bytes truncated.
